tours.title: The Architect's Triad & Principles
tours.sub: Firmitas, Utilitas, Venustas, the Vitruvian Man, and the Wind Tower

stops.note: Strength, utility, and beauty: the threefold measure of every work.
Ichnographia, orthographia, scaenographia: plan, elevation, perspective.
Homo bene figuratus: the human body in circle and square as canon of proportion.
Optical adjustments: why true symmetry must answer the eye rather than raw measure.
Andronicus of Cyrrhus and the octagonal marble Tower of the Winds at Athens.

tours.title: Temples & the Ionic Canon
tours.sub: From temple plans and Hermogenes to the 25-foot Ionic column of III.5

stops.note: Peripteral hexastyle: six columns front and rear, eleven along each flank.
Eustyle: 2¼ D intercolumniations with a 3 D central bay for approaching the cella.
Scamilli impares: swelling the stylobate upward so long horizontals do not appear hollowed.
The Ionic Order built sentence by sentence (open the interactive III.5 Plate for all 78 bindings).
Callimachus at Corinth: a maiden’s basket overgrown with acanthus births the Corinthian capital.
Sacred exposure: temples and statues look West so worshippers face the rising East.

tours.title: Forum, Basilica at Fano & Acoustic Theatre
tours.sub: Vitruvius’ own built Basilica, harmonic bronze resonators, and Roman baths

stops.note: The Italian Forum: oblong 3 : 2 proportions framed by two-storey porticoes for spectacles.
Vitruvius’ Basilica at Fano: giant 50-foot columns, clerestory lights, and Augustus’ pronaos.
Roman Theatre geometry: four equilateral triangles inscribed in the orchestra fix the scaena.
Echea: tuned bronze vessels set in mathematical harmonic ratios beneath the theatre seats.
Roman Baths: caldarium and tepidarium turned to the Southwest winter sunset, above hypocausts.
Harbours in open sea: hydraulic Campanian pozzolana hardening underwater inside oak cofferdams.

tours.title: Aqueducts, Leveling & Honest Craft
tours.sub: Finding springs, the 20-foot chorobates, inverted siphons, and frescoes

stops.note: Testing hidden water: a 3×3×5 ft pit and bronze bowl oiled at sunset to catch morning dew.
The Chorobates: a 20-foot straightedge with plummets and water channel for true leveling.
Aqueduct arcades and castellum: dividing public fountains, baths, and private houses.
The Venter: crossing deep valleys with lead-pipe inverted siphons and air vents.
Apaturius at Tralles: Licymnius refutes impossible architectural fantasies in wall painting.

tours.title: Analemma, Clocks & Ancient Machines
tours.sub: Rome’s 9:8 shadow, Ctesibius’ water organ, cranes, and Hegetor’s siege tortoise

stops.note: Archimedes in the bath: hydrostatic displacement unmasks the goldsmith’s silver alloy.
The Analemma at Rome: an 8 : 9 equinoctial shadow constructs every seasonal sundial hour.
Ctesibius’ water clock: regulated inflow lifts a cork float turning geared astronomical drums.
Colossal hoists: the treadwheel drum multiplying human force through trispast pulleys.
The Water Screw: laid out on the 3-4-5 Pythagorean right triangle.
The Hydraulis: Ctesibius’ bronze water organ balancing wind pressure under water.
Hegetor of Byzantium: the 63×42-foot siege tortoise carrying a 104-foot iron-headed ram.
